question: Is the air better in the north or the west of Singapore right now?
name: Claude
answer:
**The north has the better air.** The latest readings I could find (around midday on 16 Oct) show the north clearly ahead of the west. I can't pull NEA's live feed, so these may be a few hours old.

| Region | 24-hr PSI | 1-hr PM2.5 (µg/m³) |
|---|---|---|
| North | 153 (Unhealthy) | 152 |
| West | 202 (Very unhealthy) | 157 |

The north was also ahead in every other snapshot I found from the past day. On 15 Oct around 5pm, the north had a PSI of 122 and the west 188. Earlier that day, the north's PM2.5 was about 98 µg/m³ against about 139 in the west.

- **Haze:** This is the Kalimantan and Sumatra smoke haze. The west has been among the worst-hit regions, and the north among the best.
- **Both are still unhealthy:** Even in the north, the PSI is in the "Unhealthy" band. NEA's advice for that band is to reduce prolonged or strenuous outdoor activity, especially for children, older people and anyone with heart or lung conditions.
- **Outlook:** NEA expects the 24-hr PSI to stay "Unhealthy" to "low Very Unhealthy". Winds may shift south or south-easterly and bring more showers, which could ease the haze.

For a current reading, check the NEA website or the myENV app, which update hourly.

Sources: sgairquality.com, checkpointsg.com, hazenow.app, Yahoo News Singapore (Straits Times), AsiaOne.

SINGAPORE – Hazy conditions across Singapore worsened on Oct 16 as the hourly PM2.5 readings entered the "high" band islandwide while the PSI readings in the east, west and central regions stayed in the "very unhealthy" range.  # Haze in S’pore: Air quality worsens as PM2.5 in ‘high’ range across all regions SINGAPORE – Hazy conditions across Singapore worsened on Oct 16 as the hourly PM2.5 readings entered the "high" band islandwide while the PSI readings in the east, west and central regions stayed in the "very unhealthy" range.  Meanwhile, the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) in the central region stood at 226, after hitting a new high for this haze season of 227 at 9am. The east and the west regions recorded 205 and 202 respectively.  The north and south areas of Singapore recorded PSI readings in the unhealthy band at that time, measuring 153 and 184 respectively.    Air quality is considered unhealthy when the PSI – a 24-hour rolling average of six key air pollutants – is in the range of 101 to 200 and very unhealthy when it is in the range of 201 to 300.  In its daily haze advisory on the evening of Oct 15, the National Environment Agency (NEA) forecast that the 24-hour PSI for Oct 16 would be in the "unhealthy" to "low very unhealthy" range.  NEA said that dense smoke haze from fires in Kalimantan continued to drift towards Singapore under prevailing south-easterly winds. Smoke haze was also observed over Sumatra.  Winds are expected to shift from the south-east or south, which could reduce the smoke haze carried from Kalimantan to Singapore.  However, some smoke haze from Sumatra may still drift towards Singapore, NEA said.
